source_text: (9) Στίχ. λδ΄. Ἄνδρες κτηνοτρόφοι ἐσμέν. Βδέλυγμα Αἰγυπτίοις πᾶς ποιμὴν προβάτων, ἀλλ᾿ οὐχ Ἑβραίοις. Εἰ μὲν οὖν ὧς ποιμὴν ἐφέστηκεν ἡμῖν, βδέλυγμά ἐστιν Αἰγυπτίοις· εἱ δὲ ὡς μισθωτὸς, τάχς καὶ φίλος Αἰγυπτίοις.
thought_title: Shepherds an abomination to Egyptians but not to Hebrews
orientation: Origen is closing the work by commenting on Genesis 46:34, where Joseph's brothers tell Pharaoh they are herdsmen, and explaining why this makes them an abomination to Egyptians but not to Hebrews.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 34. [We] are men [who are] herdsmen. [An] abomination to [the] Egyptians [is] every shepherd of sheep, but not to [the] Hebrews. If therefore as [a] shepherd he has been set over us, [he] is [an] abomination to [the] Egyptians; but if as [a] hired man, quickly also [a] friend to [the] Egyptians.

lemmas.gloss: he has been set over, he has been placed in charge

choices.why: The word means keepers of livestock generally, not specifically shepherds; the distinction matters because the next clause narrows to shepherds of sheep.

choices.english: he has been set over us
choices.why: The verb means to be placed in charge or set over someone, preserving the sense of authority or oversight.
In this conditional contrast, τάχα carries the sense of 'soon' or 'readily,' marking the swift shift from abomination to friend.
The glossary requires this rendering for the ritual detestability of shepherds to Egyptians.

bible_refs.note: Ἄνδρες κτηνοτρόφοι ἐσμέν· βδέλυγμα γὰρ Αἰγυπτίοις πᾶς ποιμὴν προβάτων

pass_b_english: “We are herdsmen” (Genesis 46:34). Every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians, but not to the Hebrews. So if he has been set over us as a shepherd, he is an abomination to the Egyptians; but if he is a hired man, he is perhaps even a friend to the Egyptians.
notes: The source text reads 'τάχς' which appears to be a scribal error or OCR damage for 'τάχα'; the gloss renders it as 'quickly' based on the expected adverb.

problems.why: 'τάχα' means 'perhaps', not 'quickly' (ταχέως); this changes modality from tentative to certain.
problems.fix: perhaps even a friend to the Egyptians.

edits.old: he quickly becomes a friend to the Egyptians
edits.new: he is perhaps even a friend to the Egyptians

fixed: Changed 'quickly becomes a friend' to 'is perhaps even a friend' because the source τάχα means 'perhaps', not 'quickly' (ταχέως).

last_rejected.quote: if he has been set over us as a shepherd
last_rejected.source_quote: εἰ μὲν οὖν ὧς ποιμὴν ἐφέστηκεν ἡμῖν
last_rejected.why: Subject is 'he' but source has no explicit subject; context suggests 'one' or 'someone', not a specific person.
last_rejected.fix: if one has been set over us as a shepherd
last_rejected.ruling: ἐφέστηκεν implies a personal subject; 'he' is acceptable for generic reference in English

last_rejected.quote: if he is a hired man
last_rejected.why: Same issue: 'he' implies specific person; source uses generic 'one' or 'someone'.
last_rejected.fix: but if one is a hired man
last_rejected.ruling: μισθωτὸς is a noun; generic 'he' is normal English for unspecified person, not a mistranslation
